introduction: The phrase is the Qur’an’s: “thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops”. Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá applied it to the future of their own Faith, promising that after a slow beginning people would come in groups and then in masses; later letters distinguish the stages. This guide gathers the promises together with the conditions attached to them: each believer the companion of one other soul, and conduct that matches the teaching. The prophets’ nations flowing to the mountain, the harvest already white, the three thousand of Pentecost and the multitude no one could number are the Bible’s versions. The narrow gate, the tares among the wheat, and the history of “compel them to come in” are what a hope for numbers must reckon with.
questions: What do the readings say must happen before people enter “in troops”?
Why does the Qur’an tell the Prophet, at the moment of triumph, to seek forgiveness?
What are the risks to a small community of growing quickly?
Does the hope of large numbers change how one treats the individual in front of one?

outside.why: Beneath its banner all will gather. All nations shall flow unto it.
Each person the intimate companion of one other. Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and brought him to Jesus.
Had the friends acted on what they were told. Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord.
Humanity will enter group after group. A great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues.
Soon most of the world will be enkindled. The earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.
Grieve not; soon it will descend. Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
Others will enter later. One soweth, and another reapeth; other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours.
Its radiance will appear in future centuries. The least of all seeds becometh a tree.
Eleven believed in the time of Christ. The same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.

The readings quote this chapter: when Allah’s succour and the triumph cometh, and thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops, then hymn the praises of thy Lord, and seek forgiveness of Him.
The verse fulfilled. Large numbers bring a mixed harvest: let both grow together until the harvest. What do readings 2 and 3 suggest a community must be before it can receive many?

Greetings and a call to effort. The church’s growth by troops under Constantine came with the reading it gave this line: compel them to come in. How do the readings keep the hope of numbers from becoming pressure?
Soon you will see them enter in troops. Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, and few there be that find it. Which did Jesus expect, the few or the many, and which do the readings?

shortfall: The remaining readings repeat the promise or add later commentary on it.
